claim: The short-channel breakout is taken only when the immediately prior theoretical breakout in that market was a loser; the prior breakout is tracked even when skipped, direction is irrelevant, and a longer-channel failsafe prevents missing a major trend after a prior winner.
translation_to_code: per-symbol theoretical state machine; base entries after prev_outcome None/-1; optional longer-channel failsafe after prev_outcome +1; opposite-channel exit and 2ATR stop; completed-bar signal and next-bar fill.

claim: Test whether binary win/loss sequences in a Donchian breakout process show non-random alternation and whether conditioning on the previous theoretical trade improves a matched baseline.
translation_to_code: runs-test diagnostic plus matched all/after-loser/after-winner/turtle-failsafe comparisons on identical data, channels, stop, cost and account engine. Used only to discover the hypothesis; no 2024 rule is sourced from post-2023 material.
